correctness.rationale: Theorem 1.8 is directly verified in the publicly available primary full text. Width-one zonotopes fit in an integer-normal Euclidean slab of thickness at most one. For the exceptional unimodular class, half-cross-product facet normals are integral with determinant two and even column sum; the exact parallelotope inradius is the reciprocal of their largest norm. Integrality and determinant enforce a norm at least square root two. Equality and parity force all normal supports to be the three distinct two-coordinate supports; determinant then fixes their Gram matrix up to signs. The cofactor inverse fixes the edge Gram matrix to 4I-J. An explicit determinant-minus-one integer transformation realizes the maximizing rhombohedron, and the six independent facet tangencies fix its unique incenter. Exact finite arithmetic independently checks the matrices and bounded equality structures, but the proof does not rely on finite enumeration.
